comment: Best class I've had at UR so far. Kocher is the University Chaplain, but it's clear teaching is a calling of his. He skillfully guides in-class discussions in which everyone is welcome to share their perspective. This allows students to become friends. Reading can be heavy but is always interesting. Can't scream "TAKE THIS CLASS!" loud enough.

I absolutely adore Dr. Kocher. His class was my favorite this semester. The discussions are so interesting and I feel really bonded to my classmates and to him. Some of the readings are long but they're always very interesting. I feel like I've truly learned so much and as long as you follow his guidelines it's not too difficult to get an A.

Craig is a caring and passionate teacher with an open mindset and lots of respect from the community for his outreach in the religions dept. The class gets challenging at times with specific writing rules and sometimes-longer readings, but it's mostly just fine. However I do believe his grading style is unclear and inconsistent.
I love Dr. Kocher!!! So kind and an incredible professor. Take this class!!!

He performs the "seminar" aspect of FYS better than any professor at this school. The discussions are engaging, and he values all opinions. He's the only professor I've heard of that schedule's 1 on 1 meetings with every student, just to get to know each student. I can't say enough good things about his class.

Professor Kocher's Faith and Difference in America was a great class. The discussions were always engaging and I enjoyed being in class with him. He is definitely a tough grader, and I felt that sometimes he was very harsh with the points he took off/ not always justified, but overall the course work for the class it not too difficult.

Dr. Kocher is a fair grader and good teacher. We wrote a few papers and did one presentation, but most of the class is readings and discussion. His class is essentially an introduction to interfaith leadership and I found it very interesting. He is an understanding man and I hope to see him around campus.

Dr. Kocher genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and his passion is infectious. The class was very much discussion based, with three major papers throughout the semester. The class material is very interesting and relevant to today's society. 
As far as FYS classes go, this is a pretty good one. Highly recommend.

Definitely one of the best FYS classes to take from what I've heard about the other FYS classes. Reading and lectures are engaging, and Dr. Kocher really cares about his students. The grade is based on 3 papers, 1 presentation, a reflection paper, and a few pop quizzes.
Great professor, so kind and caring. Really makes you think about what you're learning about and has great readings.

Dr. Kocher is extremely invested in his students and their well-being. His readings are interesting and his papers/ presentations are not graded too difficult, with the added bonus of being spaced far apart. Dr. Kocher is very knowledgable and brings interesting perspective to class discussion while also empowering all his students to participate.

Solid professor that cares about his students. Some of the readings were long but others were engaging reads. Approaching issues and questions from a faith perspective (which I do much more thanks to this class) has led to hearing interesting perspectives I would not have heard otherwise.

one of my favorite professors at UR. the class I wanted to go to every week. Really cool material and he's so great at leading discussion that I feel like you learn more about yourself and your classmates. a few papers but my writing definitely improved.
Great class, great guy. He gives very specific instructions for papers, and for a good, you have to follow them exactly. A decent amount of papers with a 10-page paper at the end of the course.

Dr. Kocher is a super nice guy who cares about his students and respects everyone. Your grade in his FYS is based on a few papers and reading quizzes. You have to read a decent amount for every class and the papers aren't awful but he grades them pretty hard. Definitely more work and harder than some other FYS but not awful bc the class isn't borin

Dr. Kocher's a really nice guy who cares about his students! This class is definitely a good choice for a lax FYS. He assigns long readings, but as long as you skim and understand the context you'll pass.

Craig is a really nice guy and a really good professor. Projects are pretty easy same with pop quizzes if you read the sparknotes only thing is he grades pretty tough on papers which are pretty much your grade. Easy B for sure

Only FYS i could get into and not bad. He is a really nice guy but grades paper very by the book english professor style, not easy, not too hard. He expects a ton of reading, a full book every week, with a few racing quizzes. Only 1 person actually reads and you can get away with not reading. He's passionate and class is pretty engaging and chill.
